title: Machinery
preview: At the upper level, the windmill shows its intelligence. Wooden beams, gears, ropes and stone wheels translated the force of the wind into the flour that sustained village life.
details: Please move slowly and mind your head. The mechanism above and around you is the heart of the mill, joining the sails outside with the grinding stones inside.
The two millstones weigh more than two tons together and came from Nisyros, an island known for strong stone suited to milling. Raw wheat was poured into the feeder above the stones.

items.label: Feeder and bell
items.text: A small bell helped the miller hear when the wheat was running low.

items.label: Flour path
items.text: Finished flour passed through a pipe to the lower floor, where the miller could keep a share as payment.

items.label: Ropes and brakes
items.text: Levers slowed the stones or stopped the work quickly when needed.

items.label: Boat-like ceiling
items.text: The shape reflects local intelligence shaped by wind, wood, sea and daily work.

details: Return outside toward the threshing floor, where wheat was prepared before it reached the mill.
